label: AgMsv_1.452
cite_parts:
pūrvam eva kathaṃ tūṣṇīṃ nātiṣṭhan kiṃ vikatthanaiḥ /
ātmanaś cābhisaṃdhānavandhyasyaiva balādayam // [AgMsv_1.452]
quick_english: Why did it not stay silent before, and what do boasts avail for one barren of resolve?

label: AgMsv_1.453
cite_parts:
manokṣajālasaṃyogo bhavet kiṃ nāsamañjasaḥ /
abhisandhir athaitasya viṣayaṃ prati jāyate // [AgMsv_1.453]
quick_english: Would the union of mind and sense-net be inconsistent, and does resolve arise toward its object?

label: AgMsv_1.454
cite_parts:
ajñāte ko 'bhisandhiḥ syāj jñāte ko 'rtho 'kṣasaṃyujā /
prajñāte smaryamāṇe ced abhisandhātṛbhāvitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.454]
quick_english: If unknown, what resolve; if known, what purpose in sense-union; if remembered, it is shaped by the resolver.

label: AgMsv_1.455
cite_parts:
anyad evābhisandhātuḥ prayatno 'nyatra jāyate /
mmanoyuktātmasaṃbaddhacakṣurādyakṣasaṃśritāḥ // [AgMsv_1.455]
quick_english: The resolver's effort arises elsewhere, while senses rest on the mind-united self.

label: AgMsv_1.456
cite_parts:
viṣayāḥ savidhībhūtanetrādyullaṅghanakramāt /
ātmany eva kathaṃkāraṃ pramātṛtvaṃ pratanvatām // [AgMsv_1.456]
quick_english: How do objects, by overtaking the eye sequence, extend knowerhood in the self?

label: AgMsv_1.457
cite_parts:
nanu jñānakṛto mātṛbhāvo vijñānam ātmani /
samavaiti tato 'nyasya kathaṃ mātṛtvaśaṅkanam // [AgMsv_1.457]
quick_english: If knowledge-made motherhood occurs in the self, how can motherhood be doubted for another?

label: AgMsv_1.458
cite_parts:
etad eva vayaṃ brūmo jñānaṃ tatraiva vai kutaḥ /
bhayāt svapakṣapātāndhas tad evottaram abhyadhāt // [AgMsv_1.458]
quick_english: We say knowledge is there; why fear, O party-blind one, that reply was stated?

label: AgMsv_1.459
cite_parts:
yathendriyātmasaṃyoge manaḥ kāraṇam ucyate /
tathaivātmamanoyoge kāraṇāntaram ucyatām // [AgMsv_1.459]
quick_english: As mind is cause in sense-self union, so let another cause be said in self-mind union.

label: AgMsv_1.460
cite_parts:
tathātve cānavasthaiva mūlakṣatikarī ca sā /
atha svāntātmasaṃyogo dhruva evābhyupeyate // [AgMsv_1.460]
quick_english: In such case there is regress damaging the root; otherwise mind-self union is assumed fixed.

label: AgMsv_1.461
cite_parts:
jñātāraḥ syuḥ sadā suptamattamūrchitadurbhagāḥ /
na caitad bhavatāṃ jñānam abhīṣṭaṃ śākyaśiṣyavat // [AgMsv_1.461]
quick_english: Knowers would always be sleeping, drunk, fainted, unfortunate; this is not your desired knowledge, like a Buddhist disciple.

label: AgMsv_1.462
cite_parts:
tasmāt pratyakṣatā nāma katham indriyagocarāt /
atha pratyekam eteṣāṃ parīkṣeyaṃ pratanyate // [AgMsv_1.462]
quick_english: Therefore how is perceptibility from sense-range; then examination of these is extended.

label: AgMsv_1.463
cite_parts:
tatrāṇu nityaṃ sarvārthaṃ vegavallaghv abhautikam /
manas tac cāpi naiveha yuktisiddhatvam aśnute // [AgMsv_1.463]
quick_english: There an atomic eternal all-object swift light non-material mind is proposed, but it does not attain reason-establishedness here.

label: AgMsv_1.464
cite_parts:
aṇu cec chīgrasaṃcāri mano yad viṣayān muhuḥ /
spṛśet tadaiva dehasya bhavec chavaśarīratā // [AgMsv_1.464]
quick_english: If an atomic swift-moving mind repeatedly touched objects, the body would become a corpse.

label: AgMsv_1.465
cite_parts:
dehasthe 'pi manoyoge tatraiva jñānayogataḥ /
ekāṇumātraṃ jīvaḥ syāc chiṣṭaṃ syād ghaṭakuḍyavat // [AgMsv_1.465]
quick_english: Even in body-seated mind union, from knowledge union the soul would be only one atom, the rest like pot and wall.

label: AgMsv_1.466
cite_parts:
atha svāntena yogaś cej jātaḥ kvāpy ātmagocare /
tad vibhor ātmano jñānaṃ samavāyīti mātṛtā // [AgMsv_1.466]
quick_english: If union by mind is born somewhere in self-range, knowledge of the all-pervading self is inherent, hence motherhood.

label: AgMsv_1.467
cite_parts:
jāteti sarvadehasthaṃ jīvanaṃ kiṃ na siddhyati /
enayaiva na kiṃ yuktyā ghaṭāder jīvanaṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.467]
quick_english: Thus life in all bodies is not established; by this very reason, would pot and the like have life?

label: AgMsv_1.468
cite_parts:
vibhāv ātmani jātaṃ hi jñānaṃ tatraikadeśataḥ /
dehamātre punaḥ svānte bhavet sāvayavā sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.468]
quick_english: Knowledge born in the all-pervading self; from one part in body only, again in mind there would be a state with parts.

label: AgMsv_1.469
cite_parts:
vibhutve mānasasya syād yugapat sarvavedanam /
nitye ca manasi jñānaṃ sarvadaiva bhavet tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.469]
quick_english: If mind were all-pervasive, all perception would occur simultaneously; if mind were eternal, knowledge would always occur.

label: AgMsv_1.470
cite_parts:
mokṣāvasthāpi vijñānayoginy evopajāyate /
muktau cātmamanoyogo nāstīty etan mahādbhutam // [AgMsv_1.470]
quick_english: Even liberation state arises possessing awareness union; yet self-mind union is denied in liberation—this is a great wonder.

label: AgMsv_1.471
cite_parts:
kiṃ hi vyāpakatā mokṣe svātmano vinirudhyate /
abhautikaṃ cet sarvārthaṃ kathaṃkāraṃ mano bhavet // [AgMsv_1.471]
quick_english: Why is the pervasiveness of one's own self restricted in liberation; if mind is non-material, how can it be all-object?

label: AgMsv_1.472
cite_parts:
viśiṣṭaviṣayavyaktikauśalād eva cakṣuṣaḥ /
taijasatvam abhīṣṭaṃ hi tan mano bhautikaṃ na kim // [AgMsv_1.472]
quick_english: It asks whether mind is material, since its luminous nature is desired from skill in manifesting distinct objects.

label: AgMsv_1.473
cite_parts:
sarvarthatve ca manasaḥ kim anyair akṣaḍambaraiḥ /
nanu bāhye 'sya viṣaye prāg asty akṣopayogitā // [AgMsv_1.473]
quick_english: If mind grasps all objects, why are other sense-organs needed, since external objects already have sense-usefulness?

label: AgMsv_1.474
cite_parts:
tathā hīndriyasaṃdṛṣṭe pāścātyā manasaḥ sthitiḥ /
atrocyate yathaiva prāg indriyeṇa na gṛhyate // [AgMsv_1.474]
quick_english: Thus mind's later state is in what sense perceives; it is said that, just as earlier, it is not grasped by sense.

label: AgMsv_1.475
cite_parts:
tac cet svalakṣaṇaṃ paścād anuyantr iti kā kathā /
atha sāmānyamātraṃ tad gṛhītaṃ prāk tadindriyaiḥ // [AgMsv_1.475]
quick_english: If the particular is only inferred later, what is there to say; if only a universal was grasped earlier by those senses.

label: AgMsv_1.476
cite_parts:
vyaktiniṣṭhaṃ tadānīṃ ca manasā vyaktiniścayaḥ /
nāstīti manasā kasmāt sāmānyagrahaṇaṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.476]
quick_english: Then particular is fixed and mind determines particular; if not, why would mind grasp a universal?

label: AgMsv_1.477
cite_parts:
vinā vyaktigraheṇaiva sāmānyagrahaṇaṃ ya[ku]taḥ /
sāmānyagrahaṇe cāsya sarvārthatvaṃ nirudhyate // [AgMsv_1.477]
quick_english: Without particular grasp, from where universal grasp? And if universal grasp occurs, mind's all-objectness is destroyed.

label: AgMsv_1.478
cite_parts:
viśeṣagrahavandhyasya sarvaśabdavilopataḥ /
āśugāmitvam etasya yac coktaṃ tatra vastuni // [AgMsv_1.478]
quick_english: Deprived of particular grasp, all words vanish; the speed attributed to it in that object is thereby challenged.

label: AgMsv_1.479
cite_parts:
puraḥsthite svahastādau kiṃcid dūragate ghaṭe /
atidūre ca mervādau kathaṃ tulyaiva gantṛtā // [AgMsv_1.479]
quick_english: For an object before the hand, a somewhat distant pot, and very distant Meru, how can going-agency be equal?

label: AgMsv_1.480
cite_parts:
āśusaṃcāriṇāṃ yasmāt kvāpi pūrvakatejasām (?) /
savidhāsavidhatvena viśeṣaḥ pravibhāvyate // [AgMsv_1.480]
quick_english: Because of prior light of swift-moving things, difference by near and far is manifested.

label: AgMsv_1.481
cite_parts:
kathaṃ cābhautikaṃ sūkṣmaṃ gṛhṇīyāt parvatādikam /
abhivyaktiḥ samānasya samānena vidhīyate // [AgMsv_1.481]
quick_english: How could a non-elemental subtle thing grasp mountains and the like? Manifestation is established by the same through the same.

label: AgMsv_1.482
cite_parts:
nanv astu prākṛtī buddhis tato 'haṃkṛt tato manaḥ /
ittham apy aṇutā naiva manasaḥ saṃprasiddhyati // [AgMsv_1.482]
quick_english: Let there be material intellect, then ego, then mind; even so, mind's atomicity is not established.

label: AgMsv_1.483
cite_parts:
vyāpakatvena pūrvoktadūṣaṇāni sthitāny alam /
itthaṃ mano na yuktyaṃśair mānasāvarjanāya naḥ // [AgMsv_1.483]
quick_english: By pervasiveness the previous refutations remain; thus mind is not accepted by reason-parts for us.

label: AgMsv_1.484
cite_parts:
yādṛg vādyantarair iṣṭaṃ dvaitavyāmūḍhadṛṣṭibhiḥ /
cidātmanaḥ prakāśasya tathābhāsanabhāginī // [AgMsv_1.484]
quick_english: Such as is desired by other instruments for dualist-deluded views, so participates in the manifestation of consciousness-self.

label: AgMsv_1.485
cite_parts:
yā śaktis tan manas tv astu svasvātantryopakalpitam /
yatra śrotraṃ nabhas tatra sarvaśabdaśrutir bhavet // [AgMsv_1.485]
quick_english: Let that mind be a power imagined by self-autonomy; where ear and space are, there all sound hearing would be.

label: AgMsv_1.486
cite_parts:
cakṣurādyaiś ca sarvatra nirvibandhaṃ yato nabhaḥ /
dharmādharmair vibandhaś ca yuktyupanyāsavaikalī // [AgMsv_1.486]
quick_english: By eye and the rest perception is everywhere unobstructed because of space; obstruction by merit and demerit shows the opponent's reasoning is weak.

label: AgMsv_1.487
cite_parts:
bādhiryādi kathaṃ ca syāt kathaṃ vā taccikitsanam /
bandhāśrayavighātena tadanugrahas tathā // [AgMsv_1.487]
quick_english: How could deafness and the like arise, or how could they be treated? Thus grace comes by destroying the support of bondage.

label: AgMsv_1.488
cite_parts:
akṣaṃ svāvayaveṣv eva x x x samavāyinaḥ /
viśeṣeṇa nabho naiva kvāpy āśritam iti sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.488]
quick_english: A sense organ is inherent in its own parts; space is not dependent anywhere: this is the position.

label: AgMsv_1.489
cite_parts:
saṃyogitā tu \ldots sākaṃ bhāvena vartate /
tadanugrahaghātābhyām api vikriyatāṃ tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.489]
quick_english: Conjunction occurs together with being; by grace and destruction let it be modified then.

label: AgMsv_1.490
cite_parts:
yad anugrahas tad anugrahaḥ sa tadāśrayaḥ /
itīyaṃ svavacaḥkḷptir niḥsāraiva vibhāti naḥ // [AgMsv_1.490]
quick_english: Grace is grace and that is its support; thus this self-speech construction appears empty to us.

label: AgMsv_1.491
cite_parts:
āśrayadvārako 'kṣāṇām anugraha iti sphuṭam /
abhidhatsva ka eteṣām āśrayo 'stv iti codite // [AgMsv_1.491]
quick_english: When asked what support these senses have, favor is named as support.

label: AgMsv_1.492
cite_parts:
yad anugrahayogo 'sya sa evāśraya ity ayam /
nyāyo 'nyonyasamālambī cakrakaṃ nātivartate // [AgMsv_1.492]
quick_english: This reasoning that favor-union is support does not escape mutual dependence.

label: AgMsv_1.493
cite_parts:
vāyuprakṛti yac coktaṃ sparśanaṃ tad vivicyate /
vāyor vegavatī tāvad aniruddhā sthitiḥ sthitā // [AgMsv_1.493]
quick_english: The touch said to be air-nature is distinguished while air's swift unobstructed state remains established.

label: AgMsv_1.494
cite_parts:
dehadeśe tataḥ sparśaḥ na kuḍya iti kaḥ kramaḥ /
cakṣuś ca taijasaṃ tejaḥ prasṛtaṃ bāhyagocare // [AgMsv_1.494]
quick_english: If touch is not wall in the body-place, what order follows, while the eye is fiery light extended into external range?

label: AgMsv_1.495
cite_parts:
arthān rūpapradhānāṃś ca vettīty etan nirūpyate /
adṛśyaṃ yadi tat tejaḥ preryate manasā katham // [AgMsv_1.495]
quick_english: This examines how objects, predominantly form, are known, and how invisible light could be driven by mind.

tokens.grounds: verb third singular present active plus indeclinable

label: AgMsv_1.496
cite_parts:
preraṇaṃ na hy avijñānaṃ kadācid upapadyate /
indriyeṇa na ca jñātaṃ kadācic cākṣuṣaṃ mahaḥ // [AgMsv_1.496]
quick_english: Driving never occurs without knowledge, and visual greatness is never known merely by sense.

label: AgMsv_1.497
cite_parts:
na cāpīndriyavijñāte svatantraṃ bhavatāṃ manaḥ /
apreritaṃ ca tat paśyet sarvataḥ sarvathā sadā // [AgMsv_1.497]
quick_english: Mind is not independent in what is sense-known, and undriven mind would see everywhere in every way always.

label: AgMsv_1.498
cite_parts:
āsamañjasyam eva syāt pravṛttau vā nivartane /
kiṃ ca golakasaṃsthānaṃ tāvac ca yadi tan mahaḥ // [AgMsv_1.498]
quick_english: Inconsistency would arise in activity or cessation, and the orb-arrangement is questioned if that greatness holds.

label: AgMsv_1.499
cite_parts:
tāvatas tadgatasyaiva grahaḥ syān nānyataḥ kvacit /
tathaitad viparītaṃ tu golake 'pi nimīlite // [AgMsv_1.499]
quick_english: Grasping would be only of that gone-indeed, not from elsewhere anywhere; yet the opposite holds even in a closed orb.

label: AgMsv_1.500
cite_parts:
unmīlite vā sarvatra vastuni grahaṇaṃ bhavet /
unmīlite cakṣuṣi ca prasṛte raśmimaṇḍale // [AgMsv_1.500]
quick_english: When opened, grasping would occur everywhere in the object, and when the eye is opened with ray-circle extended.

label: AgMsv_1.501
cite_parts:
tasyāsti na paṭasyeva saṃvṛtir netramīlane /
tato nimīlitākṣasya vastudṛṣṭir na kiṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.501]
quick_english: There is no cloth-like covering in eye-closing, so closed-eyed object-sight would not occur.

label: AgMsv_1.502
cite_parts:
ghane cātapamadhye 'sti vinimīlitacakṣuṣaḥ /
citratejovabhānaṃ tatpīḍitākṣayugasya ca // [AgMsv_1.502]
quick_english: In dense sunlight there is bright light appearance for one with closed eyes and pressed eye-pair.

label: AgMsv_1.503
cite_parts:
yogināṃ bindudṛg dhvānte kathaṃ tad vā bhaviṣyati /
bhaved unmīlite 'py akṣṇi na vastugrahaṇaṃ kvacit // [AgMsv_1.503]
quick_english: How would yogins' point-sight in darkness be, when even with opened eye there is no object-grasping anywhere?

label: AgMsv_1.504
cite_parts:
manodhiṣṭhānayogena paramāṇvadhikaprathā /
dīpāpekṣā ca yāmuṣya sāpi kiṃ na vibādhyate // [AgMsv_1.504]
quick_english: By mind-seat union, atom-exceeding appearance and lamp-dependence of that too may be refuted.

label: AgMsv_1.505
cite_parts:
dīpaprakāśaḥ svāntātmanetrārtheṣūpakārakaḥ /
na pratyekaṃ manovṛtteḥ saṃskāras tena ced bhavet // [AgMsv_1.505]
quick_english: Lamp-light helps mind, self, eye, and objects, but not individually; mind-fluctuation impression would be by that if.

label: AgMsv_1.506
cite_parts:
dīpe saṃkalpyamane syād rātrau rūpaparigrahaḥ /
ātmanaḥ saṃskriyā cet syāt tasya sarvagatatvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.506]
quick_english: When a lamp is imagined at night, form-grasping would occur; self-impression would be due to its all-pervadingness.

label: AgMsv_1.507
cite_parts:
sarvadā rūpasaṃvit syāt saṃyogaḥ saṃskriyā yataḥ /
amūrtasypi nityasya ko 'nyaḥ saṃskāra ucyate // [AgMsv_1.507]
quick_english: Form-awareness would always be; conjunction is impression, so for the formless eternal what other impression is called?

label: AgMsv_1.508
cite_parts:
netropakāraś cet tarhi netradeśasthite 'rciṣi /
tejomadhyagataṃ rūpaṃ na bhāseta kadācana // [AgMsv_1.508]
quick_english: If eye-help, then form in light-middle would never shine in a flame situated in the eye-place.

label: AgMsv_1.509
cite_parts:
nanu tad vedyadeśe 'sau nāyanaḥ kiraṇavrajaḥ /
hanta tatraiva vijñānam ātmadeśe na kiṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.509]
quick_english: If the eye's rays reach the object, why should knowledge not arise in the self's own place?

label: AgMsv_1.510
cite_parts:
tatraivātmā vibhutvena tatraiva karaṇaṃ yataḥ /
tasmād bhogāśrayo deho jīvann iti vṛthoktayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.510]
quick_english: Since the self is omnipresent and the instrument is there itself, talk of the body as support of enjoyment is vain.

label: AgMsv_1.511
cite_parts:
nāyanānāṃ mayūkhānāṃ gantṛtve 'vasite sati /
anāvṛte 'raṇyamārge svahastāt prabhṛti sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.511]
quick_english: Once the going of eye-rays is settled, clear perception begins from one's own hand along an uncovered forest path.

label: AgMsv_1.512
cite_parts:
arkacandrādisaṃdṛṣṭiḥ kathaṃ nāmopajāyatām /
śīghratve 'pi yataḥ proktabhedo dūrāvidūragaḥ // [AgMsv_1.512]
quick_english: How can perception of sun and moon arise, even if swift, when the stated difference concerns going far and near?

label: AgMsv_1.513
cite_parts:
dīpanetrāvabhāsābhyāṃ channe tasmin kathaṃ matiḥ /
śuddha eva bhaved bhāve tābhyāṃ vyāmalatājuṣi // [AgMsv_1.513]
quick_english: How can mind arise when lamp and eye illumination cover it; pure being would remain in that state.

label: AgMsv_1.514
cite_parts:
andhatvaṃ tac cikitsā ca na yuktāśrayadūṣaṇā /
rasanā ca jalātmā cet taj jalaṃ srutimadyataḥ // [AgMsv_1.514]
quick_english: Blindness and its treatment are not a fault of fit support; if tongue is water-self, that water flows from the middle.

label: AgMsv_1.515
cite_parts:
tataḥ sthairyaṃ kathaṃ tasya kā ca nānārasaprathā /
tasyaikarasatāyoge tasyā naikarasasthiteḥ // [AgMsv_1.515]
quick_english: Then how is its stability possible, and what various taste manifestation occurs, if one-taste union conflicts with not-one-taste station?

label: AgMsv_1.516
cite_parts:
na syād ekarasajñaptir yathā pittabhare sati /
tiktā rasanavṛttir no mādhuryaṃ viditaṃ kṣamā // [AgMsv_1.516]
quick_english: One-taste cognition would not arise; when bile abounds, tongue function is bitter, and sweetness is not known as possible.

label: AgMsv_1.517
cite_parts:
nanu pittagataṃ taiktyaṃ na tv evaṃ rasanāgatam /
tarhi pittagūḍau tulyaṃ rasanāpathagāminau // [AgMsv_1.517]
quick_english: Bitterness is bile-gone, not tongue-gone; then bile-hidden and tongue-path-goers are equal.

label: AgMsv_1.518
cite_parts:
iti syād yugapaj jñaptis tiktamādhuryagocarā /
nīrasā rasanā cet sā rasābhivyañjikā kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.518]
quick_english: Thus cognition would be simultaneous toward bitter and sweet; if tongue is tasteless, whence does it manifest taste?

label: AgMsv_1.519
cite_parts:
svabhāvād iti ced asyāḥ ko 'yam āmbhasatāgrahaḥ /
ghrāṇaṃ ca pārthivaṃ tasya kāṭhinyaṃ kiṃ na dṛśyate // [AgMsv_1.519]
quick_english: If from nature, what is this water-ness grasp? Nose is earthly, so why is its hardness not seen?

label: AgMsv_1.520
cite_parts:
nanu gandhaguṇodreki kiṃ sa gandho na bhāsate /
nāsti tatrendriyavyaktagandhavattve tathā pramā // [AgMsv_1.520]
quick_english: If smell is quality-excessive, why does smell not shine? There is no valid cognition there in that way.

label: AgMsv_1.521
cite_parts:
nirgandham apṛthivyātmā mano gandhagrahakṣamam /
asty eva bhavatāṃ tena nānumā tādṛśā kṣamā // [AgMsv_1.521]
quick_english: Mind is smell-less and non-earth-self, yet smell-grasping-capable; such inference is not possible for you.

label: AgMsv_1.522
cite_parts:
tasmād indriyasaṃghāto bhautiko nopapadyate /
āhaṃkārikatāyāṃ tu vyāptṛtvam avibhinnatā // [AgMsv_1.522]
quick_english: Therefore an elemental sense-aggregate does not fit; but in egoity there is pervasion and non-distinctness.

label: AgMsv_1.523
cite_parts:
dehāśrayavirodhaś ca karaṇatvena cāsthitiḥ /
vāgādi yac ca karmākṣapañcakaṃ tad vivicyatām // [AgMsv_1.523]
quick_english: Body-support contradicts instrumentality and non-stability; speech and the five action-senses should be distinguished.

label: AgMsv_1.524
cite_parts:
ānābher mūrdhaparyantaṃ yaḥ samīrābhighātajaḥ /
viśeṣaḥ ko 'pi vāgātmā sa tādṛg iha kathyate // [AgMsv_1.524]
quick_english: From navel to head, wind-strike-born; what distinction is speech-self? Such is said here.

label: AgMsv_1.525
cite_parts:
tasya kāryaṃ bhavec chabdaḥ kartā ko 'tra vicāryatām /
ātmano naiva kartṛtvaṃ tathātve 'pi vibhutvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.525]
quick_english: Its work would be sound; who is the doer here, let be examined. The self has no doership, even in that state, due to omnipresence.

label: AgMsv_1.526
cite_parts:
mayā proccārite śabde tvaṃ vaktā kiṃ na jāyase /
prakṛtāv api doṣo 'yaṃ kartryāṃ kartṛtvavarjitā // [AgMsv_1.526]
quick_english: When I utter sound, why are you not speaker? Even in prakṛti this fault remains: doership is devoid of doership.

label: AgMsv_1.527
cite_parts:
karaṇasya sthitir nāsti tulye vāgindriye sati /
kathaṃ cāsphuṭasuspaṣṭabhāvaḥ śabdeṣu jāyate // [AgMsv_1.527]
quick_english: There is no fixed state of the instrument when the vocal organ is the same — so how does the indistinct-and-distinct state arise in sounds?

tokens.grounds: bhāva with the dvandva visarga to ḥ

label: AgMsv_1.528
cite_parts:
kathaṃ copāṃśusaṃjalpasmṛtyādau śabdagā bhidā /
prayatnāc cet prayatno 'pi yady utpattis tataḥ katham // [AgMsv_1.528]
quick_english: And how, in whispering, muttering, recollection and the like, is there sound-bound difference? If from effort — yet if effort too is an origination, whence then?

label: AgMsv_1.529
cite_parts:
viśeṣo jāyate hy anyo na hy anyaguṇasaṃbhavaḥ /
prayatnamāndyāmāndyābhyāṃ yena pratividhīyate // [AgMsv_1.529]
quick_english: For a further distinction arises, not born of another quality, by which — through slack and intense effort — it is met.

label: AgMsv_1.530
cite_parts:
pāṇīndriyaṃ cādadānaṃ mukhādyair grahaṇaṃ kutaḥ /
grahaṇaṃ ca kim ucyeta svīkāro yadi saṃmataḥ // [AgMsv_1.530]
quick_english: And the hand-organ gives nothing — whence then grasping by mouth and the rest? And what would be called grasping, if acceptance is what is meant?

label: AgMsv_1.531
cite_parts:
asvasya svasya karaṇaṃ svīkāra iti bhaṇyate /
svaśabdaś cātmavācī cet tatrātmā prakṛtir yadi // [AgMsv_1.531]
quick_english: Acceptance, it is said, is the making-ones-own of what is not ones own; and if the word 'own' expresses the self — with the self as the root...

label: AgMsv_1.532
cite_parts:
tan nāsty aprākṛtaṃ kiṃcid ity asvatatvaṃ kathaṃ kila /
ahaṅkāro 'py athātmā syān nāhaṃkārī kṛtir ghaṭe // [AgMsv_1.532]
quick_english: Therefore nothing is non-radical, they say — so how indeed is there non-ownness? Then ego too would be the self — yet pot-making is not egoic.

label: AgMsv_1.533
cite_parts:
ātmīyo 'yam anenaitad dūṣaṇenaiva dūṣitam /
ahaṃkārasya saṃbandhi sarvam eva hi tat svakam // [AgMsv_1.533]
quick_english: Mine — this is faulted by that very fault; for all that is related to ego is indeed its own.

label: AgMsv_1.534
cite_parts:
ātmano vyāpakasyāsti na svaṃ nāsvaṃ ca kiṃcana /
evaṃ pādendriyasyāpi samo 'yaṃ yuktivikramaḥ // [AgMsv_1.534]
quick_english: For the pervading self there is nothing own or not-own; and likewise for the foot-organ too this same stride of argument holds.

label: AgMsv_1.535
cite_parts:
deśād deśāntaraprāptyā gamanaṃ ca yad ucyate /
tattyāgarūpaṃ svīkārābhāvenaiva prasiddhyati // [AgMsv_1.535]
quick_english: And what is called going, by reaching from place to place — that is of abandoning-nature, established precisely by the absence of acceptance.

tokens.grounds: abhāva with svīkāra and eva instrumental

label: AgMsv_1.536
cite_parts:
svīkāro dūṣitaś caiṣa svīkārāṃśo 'pi yo gatau /
tasya pāṇīndriyaṃ yuktaṃ karaṇaṃ nāṅghrināmakam // [AgMsv_1.536]
quick_english: And this acceptance stands refuted — yet whatever share of acceptance there is in going, for that the hand-organ is the fit instrument, not the foot-named.

tokens.grounds: aṃśa with svīkāra visarga to o

label: AgMsv_1.537
cite_parts:
indriyāṇāṃ hi sāṃkāryam evaṃ kāryeṣu jāyate /
ata eva mahānyāyavedibhiś carame naye // [AgMsv_1.537]
quick_english: For the common task of the senses thus arises in their tasks; therefore indeed, by the knowers of the great Nyaya, in the final view.

label: AgMsv_1.538
cite_parts:
prokto gatiniṣedhāya bhūyān sadvākyaḍambaraḥ /
gataṃ na gamyate tāvad agataṃ naiva gamyate // [AgMsv_1.538]
quick_english: Proclaimed for the denial of going is the great pomp of true statements: the gone is not gone-to for now, the not-gone indeed is not gone-to.

label: AgMsv_1.539
cite_parts:
gatāgatavinirmuktaṃ nāstītyādi svake naye /
pāyvindriyaṃ ca na cchidramātraṃ koṣṭhyamarutkramāt // [AgMsv_1.539]
quick_english: Nothing free from gone-and-not-gone exists and the like, in one own view; and the anus-organ is not a mere hole — from the course of the belly-wind.

label: AgMsv_1.540
cite_parts:
utsargaḥ kila sāṃkāryaṃ tena syād iyatī sthitiḥ /
upastham indriyaṃ yac ca tasya kāryaṃ nigadyate // [AgMsv_1.540]
quick_english: Excretion, they say, is the common task — thereby stands just this position; and the sex-organ, whose task is declared...

label: AgMsv_1.604
cite_parts:
............................. /

śāmyatīti na yuktettham anumānapramāṇatā /
tadbhedavādināṃ tāvad dve māne naiva saṃgate // [AgMsv_1.604]
quick_english: It ceases is thus improper — inferential authoritativeness; for the difference-theorists, however, the two measures are simply incompatible.

label: AgMsv_1.605
cite_parts:
śabdādes tv anumānena sudhībhiḥ pariniścitam /
tasmāt svasaṃvid evaiṣā svaprakāśatayā sthitā // [AgMsv_1.605]
quick_english: But this, from sound, is ascertained by the wise through inference; therefore this self-consciousness abides in self-luminosity.

label: AgMsv_1.606
cite_parts:
mātṛmānaprameyādiprapañcaiḥ sāvabhāsate /

samullāsaḥ sindhor bahalalaharīvibhramamayaḥ prakāśaḥ śāśāṅkaḥ kumudadalanirbhedasacivaḥ /
parasyāḥ saṃvitter mitiviṣayamātṛvyatikarair vikāso yaḥ seyaṃ jagati vividhā kalpanakalā // [AgMsv_1.606]
quick_english: She shines forth with the expanses beginning with knower, measure, and object — the oceans upsurge of dense-wave play is moonlight, soft on unpierced lily-petals; the opening of supreme consciousness through the mixture of measure, object, and knower — that is, in the world, the manifold art of imagining.

tokens.grounds: prapañca with the triple compound instrumental plural
vyatikara with the triple instrumental plural

label: AgMsv_1.607
cite_parts:
tasmāt prakāśa evāyaṃ citraśaktisunirbharaḥ /
svayaṃ vicitrarūpeṇa bhāti viśvatra viśvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.607]
quick_english: Therefore this very light, full of manifold power, itself shines in manifold form — everywhere, from every side.

label: AgMsv_1.608
cite_parts:
tad ayaṃ prasphuṭābhāso lokarūpādivartmanā /
svaśaktyaṃśād vikalpākhyāt pratyakṣavyapadeśabhāk // [AgMsv_1.608]
quick_english: Then this clear shining, by way of world-form and the like, from own-power portion called imagining, shares the title perception.

label: AgMsv_1.609
cite_parts:
tathā hi devadevāṃśas tat samunmīlanaṃ dṛśaḥ /
prāṇaspandas tadaikāgryaṃ bhāvas taddharmasaṃcayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.609]
quick_english: For thus: the god-of-gods portion is the opening of vision; breath throb is one-pointedness on that; being is the collection of its properties.

tokens.grounds: aṃśa with devadeva visarga to s
spanda with prāṇa visarga to s

label: AgMsv_1.610
cite_parts:
ityādi sarvaṃ yad bhāti tat pratyakṣam iti sphuṭam /
na tv atra kartṛkarmāṃśakaraṇatvādinā gatiḥ // [AgMsv_1.610]
quick_english: All that shines, beginning with thus — that is clearly perception; but here there is no recourse through agent-act-part-instrumentality and the like.

tokens.grounds: tvādi with the long compound instrumental

label: AgMsv_1.611
cite_parts:
nanv asāv asti pāścātye vaikalpikapathe tataḥ /
yato dehaghaṭābhāso sphuṭaḥ paścāt tu so 'sphuṭaḥ // [AgMsv_1.611]
quick_english: But surely it exists in the later conceptual path — since the body-pot shining is clear, but afterwards it is unclear.

label: AgMsv_1.612
cite_parts:
sa eva cchannarūpas tu śuddhāṃśasvātmasaṃvidam /
tato dehaghaṭābhāsas tatrāpy eṣaiva vartanī // [AgMsv_1.612]
quick_english: But that very one of hidden form — toward pure-part self-consciousness; thence the body-pot shining; therein too this very procedure.

label: AgMsv_1.613
cite_parts:
yāvatsahasradehaughabhāvakoṭyavabhāsanam /
tatrāpi ca purā paścān na tu tādṛkprathā yadi // [AgMsv_1.613]
quick_english: Even the shining of crores of beings in thousand-fold floods of bodies — yet therein too, before and after, if there is no such-like forth-arising...

label: AgMsv_1.614
cite_parts:
āmarśapadavīṃ yāti tat spuṭāsphuṭacitritaḥ /
tāvān asāv eka eva svarūpaprasphuṭātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.614]
quick_english: It reaches the path of relishing — variegated clear-and-unclear; so much is this one alone, of manifest own-nature.

tokens.grounds: spuṭa for sphuṭa with dvandva adjective

label: AgMsv_1.615
cite_parts:
śivaprakāśa āyāti. /

\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ vicitro 'yaṃ na vastutaḥ /
tatrātadrūpasaṃveśād vaicityraṃ paricarcyate // [AgMsv_1.615]
quick_english: Śivas light comes. Variegated is this, not in reality — therein, from entry into the not-that-form, variety is considered.

label: AgMsv_1.616
cite_parts:
śivaprakāśe 'tadrūpapraveśas tu na saṃgataḥ /
yadi vā kathitanyāyabalāt kvāpi na citratā // [AgMsv_1.616]
quick_english: But entry into the not-that-form in Śivas light is incoherent — or else, by force of the stated reasoning, nowhere is there variety.

tokens.grounds: praveśa with atadrūpa visarga to s

label: AgMsv_1.617
cite_parts:
kiṃtu citratayābhāsaś citrabhāvaṃ prasūyate /
evaṃ caitro 'yam asmākaṃ citravadbhavann īdṛśaḥ // [AgMsv_1.617]
quick_english: But shining-as-variety gives birth to the variegated state; thus this Caitra of ours, being as it were variegated, is such.

tokens.grounds: ābhāsa with citratā visarga to ś

label: AgMsv_1.618
cite_parts:
maitreṇa tanmatenālaṃ dṛṣṭo māṃ bhāvadarśinam /
paśyan paśyati yaḥ so 'yaṃ samādhau pariniṣṭhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.618]
quick_english: Enough of Mitra view of that! Seen — me, the seer of beings — seeing, he sees; who, this very one, is established in samadhi.

label: AgMsv_1.619
cite_parts:
prāk tv eṣa janmakoṭīṣu tattattāpādy abhuṅkta vai /
mokṣyate dhyānacaryādyair yo 'py etena pathāgataḥ // [AgMsv_1.619]
quick_english: But formerly this one enjoyed, bringing about this and that, through crores of births indeed; he will be freed by meditation-practice and the like — whoever has come by this path.

label: AgMsv_1.620
cite_parts:
so 'py anyo mokṣabhāg īttham aparyavasitodayaḥ /
prakāśa eka evāyaṃ yaś cirān na vibhidyate // [AgMsv_1.620]
quick_english: This one too — another — is a freedom-sharer, thus of unended rise: the light, one alone, which has long been undivided.

label: AgMsv_1.621
cite_parts:
ata eva hi bhedo 'sti na kaścid yo maheśvaram /
advayaṃ saṃprabindhīta prakāśānandasundaram // [AgMsv_1.621]
quick_english: Therefore indeed there is no difference which could split the nondual Great Lord, beautiful with the bliss of light.

label: AgMsv_1.622
cite_parts:
deśakālākṛtijñānadharmopādhyantarādayaḥ /
saṃmatā bhedakatvena bhānti cet sā vibhā tathā // [AgMsv_1.622]
quick_english: Beginning with place, time, form, knowledge, property, and other adjuncts — agreed; if they shine as difference-makers, that shining is just so.

label: AgMsv_1.623
cite_parts:
na ced vibhaiva sā tādṛk tad advaitam idaṃ sphuṭam /
bheda ity eṣa śabdas tu kevalaṃ pratibhojjhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.623]
quick_english: But if that shining is just such, then this nondualism is clear — while the mere word difference is devoid of shine.

label: AgMsv_1.624
cite_parts:
astu vā bhedakalanā pratibhāsaṃprarohiṇī /
uktanītyā tu tatraiva sapratiṣṭhā bhaviṣyati // [AgMsv_1.624]
quick_english: Let there be difference-reckoning growing in shining — but by the stated reasoning it will be well-established right there.

label: AgMsv_1.625
cite_parts:
ayaṃ ghaṭaḥ paṭaś cāyaṃ tāv anyonyavibhedinau /
pramātrantarabhinnau ca tau matto 'pi vibhedinau // [AgMsv_1.625]
quick_english: This pot and this cloth — the two differ mutually, differ from another knower too, and those two differ even from me.

label: AgMsv_1.626
cite_parts:
iti prakāśa eko 'yaṃ tathāmarśasvarūpakaḥ /
nanv evaṃ pakṣapāto 'yam advaitaṃ bhavatāṃ katham // [AgMsv_1.626]
quick_english: Thus this one light, of the nature of such relishing — but surely on this view this is partiality: how is nondualism yours?

label: AgMsv_1.627
cite_parts:
bhedo 'py astu sa āhatya kiṃ nāma na viṣahyate /
seyaṃ badhiragoṣṭhīṣu gītavādyaprarocanā // [AgMsv_1.627]
quick_english: Let difference be — having struck, what indeed is not endured? This is delighting deaf assemblies with song and music.

label: AgMsv_1.628
cite_parts:
na hy advayaṃ dvayāveśabādhenāsmābhir ucyate /
tvatpakṣopagamo hy eṣa syād dvayaṃ taddhi susphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.628]
quick_english: For nondualism is not stated by us through exclusion of dualism entry — that would be reaching your side, for that dualism is blatant.

tokens.grounds: bādha with the long compound instrumental

label: AgMsv_1.629
cite_parts:
idaṃ dvaitam idaṃ neti tad idaṃ ca dvayādvayam /
iti yatra samaṃ bhāti tad advayam udāhṛtam // [AgMsv_1.629]
quick_english: This is dual, this is not, and this is dual-and-nondual — where all shines the same, that is called nondual.

label: AgMsv_1.630
cite_parts:
nanv ittham astu bhedo 'pi na vayaṃ śabdakāmukāḥ /
astv asau na hi no heyam ādeyaṃ vā yathātra vaḥ // [AgMsv_1.630]
quick_english: Well then, so be it — even difference; we are no lovers of mere words. Let it be — for us there is nothing to reject or accept, as with you here.

label: AgMsv_1.631
cite_parts:
sarvānugrāhakaṃ pakṣam ālilambiṣase yadi /
paramādvayadṛṣṭiṃ tat saṃśrayeḥ śaraṇaṃ mahat // [AgMsv_1.631]
quick_english: If you would cling to the all-favoring position, then resort to the supreme-nondual view — the great refuge.

label: AgMsv_1.632
cite_parts:
etad aṣṭādaśe tattvam adhikāre bhaviṣyati /
yat tad ante paraprāpyaṃ tad astu paramārthataḥ // [AgMsv_1.632]
quick_english: This principle will be in the eighteenth chapter — which is finally to be reached as supreme; let that ultimately be.

label: AgMsv_1.633
cite_parts:
atra ye na hi viśrāntās te mitāṃ saṃvidaṃ śritāḥ /
sarvathaivāpabādhyante janmamṛtyūtthavibhramaiḥ // [AgMsv_1.633]
quick_english: But those who here have not come to rest resort to measured consciousness; they are in every way refuted by birth-death-born delusions.

tokens.grounds: vibhrama with the compound instrumental plural

label: AgMsv_1.634
cite_parts:
tasmāt sa eka evāsau prakāśaḥ parameśvaraḥ /
pratyakṣam iti tenaiva prakāśenaiva bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.634]
quick_english: Therefore this one light alone is the Lord; directly — thus by that very light it shines.

label: AgMsv_1.635
cite_parts:
tatra tā dṛṣṭayaḥ sarvā mahānadya ivārṇave /
viśanty avaśyaṃ nāviṣṭāḥ prayānti kṛtakṛtyatām // [AgMsv_1.635]
quick_english: Therein all those views, like great rivers in the ocean, necessarily enter; unentered, they do not reach fulfillment.

label: AgMsv_1.636
cite_parts:
tathā hi mānasāmagrī rūpālokamanokṣajā /
sākaṃ mātṛprameyābhyāṃ tadvarjaṃ vāpy anekaśaḥ // [AgMsv_1.636]
quick_english: For thus the mental apparatus, born of form, light, mind, and eye — together with knower and object, or excluding that, manifoldly.

tokens.grounds: jā born with the quadruple adjective

label: AgMsv_1.637
cite_parts:
jñātaṃ ca gamayen mānaṃ na cāpi ujjhati mānatām /
pratyakṣapādotprekṣeyam idānīm upapadyate // [AgMsv_1.637]
quick_english: And let it make the measure known — nor does it abandon measureness; this perception-grounded supposition holds good now.

label: AgMsv_1.638
cite_parts:
kiṃ cānadhigatagrāhi mānaṃ navanavaṃ yataḥ /
bhairavecchāvaśād etad viśvaṃ bhāti tathā tathā // [AgMsv_1.638]
quick_english: And since the measure grasping the ungrasped is ever fresh — by Bhairavas will this universe shines just so.

label: AgMsv_1.639
cite_parts:
vastu pradarśayan mānaṃ pravṛttiṃ vidadhat sphuṭam /
prāpayaty eva tad vastu tathābhāsanayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.639]
quick_english: Displaying the thing, the measure clearly effects activity; it brings about just that thing through fitness for such shining.

label: AgMsv_1.640
cite_parts:
sad apy ekāntato nedaṃ nāsac cetyādisaṃvidaḥ /
bhānty eva paramārthena tad anekāntadṛk sphuṭā // [AgMsv_1.640]
quick_english: Even the true absolute is not simply this or nonexistence; consciousness shines ultimately through a clear non-one-sided view.

label: AgMsv_1.641
cite_parts:
eko bhāvaḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvaḥ sarve bhāvā ekabhāvasvabhāvāḥ /
arhadvādaḥ so 'yam asmadsudṛṣṭau yuktaś ca śrīsāraśāstre 'pi coktaḥ // [AgMsv_1.641]
quick_english: One being is the nature of all beings and all beings are the nature of one; this jain doctrine is fitting in our good view and is also stated in the Sri Sara scripture.

label: AgMsv_1.642
cite_parts:
idaṃ mānaṃ meyaṃ tad idam iti saṃkhyāṃ kalayituṃ svarūpaṃ vā śaktaḥ ka iva jagatīty etad api sat /
mataṃ vācāṃ patyur bhagavati cidānandasubhage yatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvād apara iha kaḥ kiṃ prakurutām // [AgMsv_1.642]
quick_english: Who is able to count measure and measured, this and that, in the world? This true opinion belongs to the blessed lord of speech, blissful consciousness; since he is silent, what else can anyone do here?

label: AgMsv_1.643
cite_parts:
ahetor bhāne syād yadi na tanudikkālaniyamas tato hetor īdṛṅ niyama iti kasyaiṣa mahimā /
svabhāvo 'yaṃ hetor atha vivṛtakaṇṭhaṃ katham asau na bhāvasyaivokto yamayati pare kena hi paraḥ // [AgMsv_1.643]
quick_english: If appearance were without cause, there would be no space-time restriction; then whose greatness is such restriction of cause? This own nature of cause, how does it not restrain being itself in the supreme, by whom indeed is the supreme?

label: AgMsv_1.644
cite_parts:
svabhāvāc cātmāsau paramaśiva ity āgamakathā nirukto viśvātmā jagati nikhile jṛmbhata iti /
dharādeś cānanyo bhavatu tad iyaṃ bhūtacititā sa vandhyo dikkālair jananamaraṇāpāyarahitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.644]
quick_english: From own nature the self is supreme Shiva, as scripture says; the world-self expands in the entire world. Let it be not other than earth and so on; this element-consciousness is barren, free from space-time, birth, death, and loss.

label: AgMsv_1.645
cite_parts:
tad asyāyaṃ lokas tadanu paraloko 'py ayam it grahaḥ kasmād dhetoḥ spṛśati na hi taṃ kālakalanā /
tataḥ svātantryodyatsukharasaparānandamahimābhavadbhasmībhūtākhilakaluṣapāśaughasubhagaḥ // [AgMsv_1.645]
quick_english: That is this world, then the other world also is this; why, because of cause, does time-measure not touch him? Therefore autonomy, rising bliss, supreme joy, glory, becoming ash, all impurity and bond-masses, is auspicious.

label: AgMsv_1.646
cite_parts:
sāṃkhyadṛk punar ihaiva bhūyasā carcyate nikhilatattvagocarā /
dṛśyate dharaṇīprabhṛty alaṃ tac ca sūkṣmatamakāraṇotthitam // [AgMsv_1.646]
quick_english: The sankhya view is again discussed here greatly, covering all principles; it is seen from earth upward, enough, and that arises from the subtlest cause.

label: AgMsv_1.647
cite_parts:
tadgṛhītikaraṇodyataṃ punar bāhyataḥ karaṇakaṃ daśātmakam /
āntaraṃ trividham asya kāraṇaṃ saukhyaduḥkhaparimohadarpaṇaḥ // [AgMsv_1.647]
quick_english: The instrument for grasping that is again external tenfold and internal threefold; the cause of this is a mirror of pleasure, pain, and delusion.

label: AgMsv_1.648
cite_parts:
tādṛśaṃ triguṇam eva yad bhavet tat punar jaḍatayātha bhedataḥ / mūlakāraṇam apekṣate paraṃ sā niśeyam iha bhogyam ucyate /
tac ca bhoktṛ paratantratāmayam no parasparam upaiti bhoktṛtām // [AgMsv_1.648]
quick_english: Such a three-guna thing, by inertness and difference, requires a supreme root cause; that is called enjoyable here, and dependence-nature does not mutually approach enjoyership.

label: AgMsv_1.649
cite_parts:
bhogyabhoktṛvapur ekam eva no jāghaṭīti hi viruddhadharmataḥ /
tena bhoktṛ citiśaktimātrakam tac cidātmamayatāvaśān manaḥ // [AgMsv_1.649]
quick_english: The body of enjoyable and enjoyer is not one, because of opposite qualities; therefore the enjoyer is only consciousness power, and mind is by consciousness nature.

label: AgMsv_1.650
cite_parts:
vyāptṛ sarvagatam īśvaraṃ kathaṃ bhoktṛtāṃ vrajatu bhedasaṃgatām /
tena tannijavaśitvanirmitāṃ saṃkucatsthitijuṣaṃ daśāṃ śrayet // [AgMsv_1.650]
quick_english: How can the all-pervading pervader, the lord, go to enjoyership joined with difference? Therefore he may resort to a contracted condition made by his own mastery.

label: AgMsv_1.651
cite_parts:
anyakāraṇakalādyabhāvataḥ so 'yam asya sahajo malaḥ smṛtaḥ /
sa tridhā samavabhāti tadvaśād eṣa eva sa pumān udāhṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_1.651]
quick_english: From absence of other cause and arts, this innate impurity of this is remembered; it appears threefold, and by its power this person is indeed called.

label: AgMsv_1.652
cite_parts:
bhoktṛbhāvaparatantratāvaśā nāntarīyakatayāsya kañcukam /
bhāti naivam iti kālavitkalārāgasanniyatināmadheyakam // [AgMsv_1.652]
quick_english: By dependence of enjoyership and by non-essentiality of this, the covering shines; not thus, it is named time, knowledge, arts, attachment, restriction.

label: AgMsv_1.653
cite_parts:
yady ātmaiṣa punar nirargalanijasvātantryasaṃchāditaṃ svaṃ rūpaṃ vivṛṇoty alaṃ nijabalāt tacchuddhavitsaṃbhavaḥ /
kartṛtvaṃ kila kāryavargam akhilaṃ bodhe nidhāya svake paśyann īśvaratāṃ vrajed aham idaṃ sarvaṃ sadety uddhuraḥ // [AgMsv_1.653]
quick_english: If this self again reveals its own form covered by own autonomy, by own strength, pure consciousness birth; agency indeed places all class of actions in own knowledge, seeing, may go to lordship: I, this all, true, exalted.

label: AgMsv_1.654
cite_parts:
jñātṛtvaṃ hṛdayāntarasphuritadṛg dṛṣṭvā sphuṭābhāsini jñeye bhedatirodhitāṃ nijacitau yasmāt sa saṃpaśyati /
tenāsyedam ahaṃvidoḥ sarabhasaṃ bhedaikyam ājagmuṣī sāmānādhikaraṇyadhīḥ prakaṭayet sādāśivīṃ saṃsthitim // [AgMsv_1.654]
quick_english: Having seen knower-ness with the eye throbbing in the hearts interior — in the clearly shining object the concealment of difference in own consciousness — since he fully sees, thereby may the thought of common-substratum-ness, swiftly attaining the unity-and-difference of I and knower, reveal the Sadāśiva-state.

tokens.grounds: dṛś with the long compound instrumental

label: AgMsv_1.655
cite_parts:
jñeyaṃ kāryaṃ sarvam antar vibodhe yāval līnaṃ tāvad udriktavṛtteḥ /
bodhajvālāsaṃcayasyāntarāle tatprastyānaṃ svaṃ vapuḥ projjhatīva // [AgMsv_1.655]
quick_english: The whole object-effect merged within awakening — insofar as merged, from exuberant activity — in the interval of the flame-mass of awakening, that setting-forth as it were abandons its own form.

label: AgMsv_1.656
cite_parts:
idaṃbhāvaḥ so 'yaṃ vigalitumanā no vigalito bhavet prākkakṣyāyām api sa samakāntis tad adhunā /
ahaṃbhāgodreke vidhir anavadhir bhāvavisare tad eṣā śāktī bhūriṣir iti svasiddhātmani parā // [AgMsv_1.656]
quick_english: This this-ness of melted mind — may it not melt away for us even in the prior stage; it is of equal lustre. That now: in the excess of the I-share the rule is boundless; in the spread of beings, this śakti — supreme in the self-proved self.

label: AgMsv_1.657
cite_parts:
īhate galitumanvato galet tatra pūrvapararūpasaṃgateḥ /
śāktabhūmir akhileyam ucyate citracinnicayacarcitā satī // [AgMsv_1.657]
quick_english: It strives — may it melt from melted thought — from the conjunction of prior-and-later form; all this is called the śākta stage, being anointed with manifold consciousness-heaps.

tokens.grounds: carcitā with the long compound feminine

label: AgMsv_1.658
cite_parts:
tattve tattve svecchayā devadevaḥ sarvāṃ sarvāṃ bhūmim ālambamānaḥ /
pūrṇaikātmā pūrṇasaṃvitsvarūpaḥ śrīmāñ śāstre bhairavo niruktaḥ // [AgMsv_1.658]
quick_english: In principle after principle, by own will, the god of gods rests upon every stage — of full one-self, of full-consciousness-nature, glorious; in scripture declared Bhairava.

label: AgMsv_1.659
cite_parts:
śaktipātadṛg iyaṃ nirucyate mandamadhyaparatīvrabhedataḥ /
tatparasparabhidābhir apy alaṃ yā svarūpaparidṛṣṭir ātmanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.659]
quick_english: This descent-of-power view is declared according to faint, middling, supreme, and intense distinction — but enough of those mutual divisions, which is the all-round vision of the self nature.

label: AgMsv_1.660
cite_parts:
nanu kiṃ kadācid ayam īśvaro nijarūpaṃ prakāśayati pūrṇacitiḥ /
kiṃ vā kadācid atha saṃvṛṇute nirhetuko hi niyamaḥ kila kaḥ // [AgMsv_1.660]
quick_english: But surely — does this Lord, full consciousness, ever reveal his own form? Or does he ever conceal it? For what indeed would be a causeless rule?

label: AgMsv_1.661
cite_parts:
uktam atra kila pūrvam anantaṃ nānyad asti niyameṣu nimittam /
laukikeṣv api sa eva maheśaś citracitraparibhāsanaśīlaḥ // [AgMsv_1.661]
quick_english: Endlessly declared before, they say: there is no other cause in regularities, even worldly ones — that very Great Lord, whose habit is ever-variegated shining-forth.

tokens.grounds: śīla with the long compound nominative

label: AgMsv_1.662
cite_parts:
tatsvātantryād adhikam adhunā nottaraṃ bambhaṇīmaḥ saṃvitsindhoḥ prathitalaharīharmyadhārādhirūḍhiḥ /
śāntis tasyās tadanu tad ayaṃ bandhanāmnāpadiṣṭas tenaivetthaṃ parigataraso mokṣa ity uktarūpaḥ // [AgMsv_1.662]
quick_english: From his autonomy — more now, no reply — we babble, mounted on the palace-course of the famed waves of the consciousness-ocean. Peace thereof; thereupon that — this one designated by the name bondage — thereby thus of fully-drunk relish: freedom, of the stated form.

tokens.grounds: adhirūḍhi with the long compound nominative
apadiṣṭa with bandhanāman visarga to s

label: AgMsv_1.663
cite_parts:
sadā kadācid adhunā tadetyādi ca saṃvidaḥ /
tatsvātantryāvabhāsīyakālakelivikalpanāḥ // [AgMsv_1.663]
quick_english: Always, sometimes, now, beginning with that — of consciousness: the time-sport imaginings shining with his autonomy.

tokens.grounds: vikalpanā with the long compound nominative plural

label: AgMsv_1.664
cite_parts:
na ca kālakalābhiḥ sa spṛśyate parameśvaraḥ /
na hi tāsāṃ svatantrāsti sthitis tatkalpanāṃ vinā // [AgMsv_1.664]
quick_english: And the Lord is not touched by time-divisions — for they have no independent standing without the imagining of that.
